plan.hypothesis: Increasing control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight from the incumbent 0.05 toward the frozen upper bound 0.10, keeping control/recipe/terminal_tip_speed_weight fixed at 0.05, lowers nominal holding_max_speed_m_s below 0.012750255515948416 m/s while keeping holding_max_error_m and terminal_error_m at or below 0.01 m.
plan.rationale: Frozen control domains admit only control/recipe/{terminal,holding}_tip_speed_weight in [0.025,0.1]; both are 0.05 in the incumbent. The holding term is a per-second squared normalized world tip speed on nodes at/after the fixed settling-window start (0.3-0.35 s), so it is the direct pressure on the only failed component (holding speed). Mathematical support is limited: a monotone penalty term is expected to lower in-window tip speed, but the effect on the sampled maximum and its interaction with position/terminal cost is not analytically guaranteed, and the incumbent already passes, so only response direction and trade-off can be observed. Two interior points 0.075 and 0.10 bracket the lever for a within-batch slope estimate; per-batch backend cap is two. No robustness or superiority claim is licensed because perturbation cases are unexecutable and near_z_plus is a non-matched subsequent event.

decision.reasoning: Current feedback: the incumbent nominal execution 91c3ba1b01d6499fb26df8f95409401b is accepted (F104=true) with holding_max_speed 0.012750255515948416 m/s vs limit 0.02 (F14<F31), holding_max_error 0.0027300544346297905 m and terminal_error 0.002697828858325615 m, both under 0.01 (F1,F108), coverage true (F100), solver errors 0 (F115). The only exposed non-matched subsequent event (near_z_plus, candidate shared-path-v11-near-section-096) is a valid_failure (F75) driven solely by holding speed 0.06758272073425946 m/s > 0.02 (F46>F31, F92=false). Because the perturbation cases are unavailable for execution in this pilot and only nominal is runnable, the robust question cannot be answered by structure change; instead the targeted, cheapest testable control-response uncertainty is whether the frozen holding-window tip-speed penalty actually lowers in-window tip speed. Both control paths lie in frozen [0.025,0.1]; I vary only control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight above the incumbent 0.05, holding terminal_tip_speed_weight fixed at 0.05. Two interior points bracket the lever and estimate slope within the two-backend per-batch cap, leaving two solves for feedback and the final decision.
unresolved_uncertainties: Incumbent robustness to the four frozen perturbation cases is untested and not executable in this pilot.
Whether a stronger holding penalty reduces holding speed monotonically and without a position trade-off is unknown.
The near_z_plus event involves a different candidate identity, so it cannot be compared to the incumbent.
No repeatability or variance evidence exists for any configuration.
